domains.name: Mileage
domains.comment:
[Definition]
Odometer reading in miles. The SBVR-era sources state the service interval in miles (R14, "5.000 miles intervals"), so the model keeps one unit for every distance; the 40,000 km disposal limit of the original case study (R21) is applied as 25,000 miles (24,855 rounded). Service Mileage uses the same unit.

domains.name: Purchase Date
domains.comment:
[Definition]
Calendar date on which a car was bought for the EU-Rent fleet.

domains.name: Registration Number
domains.comment:
[Definition]
The number plate of the car as issued by its country of registration, prefixed with the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of that country and a hyphen, because a plate is unique only within the country that issued it: NL-G-482-TK, BE-2-XYZ-123, DE-D-AB-1234. The plate is written as issued. Dutch plates follow the series issued since 2019, one letter, three digits, two letters, without vowels; Belgian plates since 2010 are an index digit, three letters and three digits; German plates start with the district code (D for Dusseldorf), then one or two letters and up to four digits. Under R21 no fleet car is older than one year, so every plate belongs to the currently issued series of its country. The value pattern covers the three countries in the sample; another country needs the pattern extended.
[Pattern]
Value pattern (regular expression) for the three countries in the sample: ^(NL-[B-DF-HJ-NP-TV-Z]-[0-9]{3}-[B-DF-HJ-NP-TV-Z]{2}|BE-[12]-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{3}|DE-[A-Z]{1,3}-[A-Z]{1,2}-[0-9]{1,4})$ . Recorded as a note because this CaseTalk build does not store a value pattern on a label type.

domains.name: Service Mileage
domains.comment:
[Definition]
Odometer reading, in miles, at the moment the car was serviced. Same unit as Mileage.

tables.name: Advance Rental
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A rental booked before the pick-up date. Subtype of Rental, defined by state: a rental that is in state Requested and whose pick-up date is in the future. EU-Rent supports both advance bookings and walk-in rentals.
[Derivation]
Advance Rental := Rental R WHERE Rental State[R].Rental Status = 'Requested' AND Rental Period[R].Pick Up Date > TODAY. Never asserted: it follows from the state and the pick-up date.
tables.verbalization:
[Rules]
"<Advance Rental> is identified by <Rental Number>"
"<Advance Rental> is a subset of <Rental Number> in <Rental>"

tables.name: Branch
tables.comment:
[Definition]
An EU-Rent site from which cars are rented out and to which they are returned. A branch belongs to exactly one local area. The same object type plays the pick-up role and the drop-off role of a rental; when the two differ the rental is a one-way rental.
[Example]
AMS01 - Amsterdam Schiphol; AMS02 - Amsterdam Centraal; BRU01 - Brussels Airport; DUS01 - Dusseldorf Hbf.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is called <Name of Branch_Branch Name><EU-Rent Network_Branch Code>"
  " belongs to <Local Area of Branch_Local Area Code><EU-Rent Network_Branch Code>"
  " is situated in <Branch City><EU-Rent Network_Branch Code>"
[Rules]
"<Branch> is identified by <Branch Code>"
"<Local Area Code> in <Branch> is a subset of <Local Area Code> in <Local Area>"

tables.name: Car
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A physical vehicle in the EU-Rent fleet, identified by its registration number. A car is of exactly one car model, is stationed at a branch, carries an odometer reading and is always in exactly one condition.
[Example]
NL-G-482-TK, a Volkswagen Polo stationed at AMS01, purchased 2025-11-03, odometer 23800, condition Available.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is stationed at <Home Branch of Car_Branch Code><EU-Rent Fleet_Registration Number>"
  " has odometer reading <Car Odometer Reading_Mileage><EU-Rent Fleet_Registration Number>"
  " is of model <Car Model of Car_Model Name><Car Model of Car_Manufacturer><EU-Rent Fleet_Registration Number>"
  " was purchased on <Purchase Date of Car_Purchase Date><EU-Rent Fleet_Registration Number>"
  " is in condition <Car Condition><EU-Rent Fleet_Registration Number>"
[Rules]
"<Car> is identified by <Registration Number>"
"<Model Name>, <Manufacturer> in <Car> is a subset of <Model Name>, <Manufacturer> in <Car Model>"
"<Branch Code> in <Car> is a subset of <Branch Code> in <Branch>"

columns.name: Purchase Date of Car_Purchase Date
columns.comment:
[Definition]
The date on which EU-Rent bought the car and it entered the fleet. Every car has exactly one purchase date. It is the date R21 measures the car's age from: a car is sold when it is one year old, or earlier when it reaches 40,000 km.
[Source]
Verbatim from the original case study: "Cars are to be sold when they reach one year old or 40,000 kilometers, whichever occurs first." - Appendix D "Case Study: EU-Rent Car Rentals" (developed by Model Systems Ltd., example by John Hall) of the Business Rules Group / GUIDE Business Rules Project final report "Defining Business Rules ~ What Are They Really?" (1995; rev. 1.3 July 2000). https://www.businessrulesgroup.org/first_paper/BRG-whatisBR_3ed.pdf . Not in the SBVR-era retellings the rest of the model was built from; those give the service interval in miles (R14), so the model keeps one unit, miles, and applies 40,000 km as 25,000 miles (24,855 rounded).

tables.name: Car Group
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A class of car models that share a rental tariff. A customer rents a car group, never a particular car: the requested car group is what the rental promises, and the car allocated at pick-up must be in that group or a higher one.
[Source]
EU-Rent: "each car is of a given model; car models are grouped into car groups; all cars in a car group have the same rental tariff." https://kdmanalytics.com/sbvr/sbvr_intro_2.html
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is described as <Description of Car Group_Car Group Description><EU-Rent Fleet_Car Group Code>"
[Rules]
"<Car Group> is identified by <Car Group Code>"

columns.name: Description of Car Group_Car Group Description

tables.name: Car Model
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A make and model of car that EU-Rent operates. Identified by the pair (manufacturer, model name) - a composite identification, expressed by the uniqueness constraint spanning both label roles of "Car Model Identification".
[Example]
Volkswagen Polo (group A); Opel Astra (group B); Volvo V60 (group D); BMW 5 Series (group E).
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is classified in <Car Group of Car Model_Car Group Code><EU-Rent Fleet_Model Name><Manufacturer>"
[Rules]
"<Car Model> is identified by <Model Name> and <Manufacturer>"
"<Car Group Code> in <Car Model> is a subset of <Car Group Code> in <Car Group>"

references.fromcolumn: Car Group of Car Model_Car Group Code

tables.name: Country
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A country in which EU-Rent operates. Countries matter to the model because the rental tariff of a car group is set per country, and because taking a car across a national border affects insurance cover.
[Example]
NL - Netherlands; BE - Belgium; DE - Germany; FR - France.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is named <Name of Country_Country Name><EU-Rent Network_Country Code>"
[Rules]
"Each <Country Name> is related to at most one <Country Code>"
"<Country> is identified by <Country Code>"

tables.name: Customer
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A person who contracts rentals with EU-Rent and is liable for the charges. Subtype of Person. A customer need not drive: the renter and the driver are separate roles.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is a customer of EU-Rent<EU-Rent Parties_Person Number>"
[Rules]
"<Customer> is identified by <Person Number>"
"<Customer> is a subset of <Person Number> in <Person>"
"<Customer> is a subset of <Person Number> in <Customer Credit Card>"

tables.name: Customer Credit Card
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " guarantees payment with card <Credit Card Number><Customer_Person Number>"
[Rules]
"<Customer Credit Card> is identified by <Credit Card Number>"
"<Person Number> in <Customer Credit Card> is a subset of <Customer>"

tables.name: Driver
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A person qualified to drive an EU-Rent car, holding a driving licence. Subtype of Person. A driver may be barred from renting after bad experiences.
[Source]
EU-Rent: "each rented car has one or more registered drivers", and EU-Rent "may bar drivers who cause bad experiences". https://caminao.blog/community/sample-problems/eu-rent-car/
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " holds a licence valid until <Licence Expiry Date><EU-Rent Parties_Person Number>"
  " holds driving licence <Driving Licence_Licence Number><EU-Rent Parties_Person Number>"
  " is a qualified driver<EU-Rent Parties_Person Number>"
[Rules]
"Each <Licence Number> is related to at most one <Driver>"
"<Driver> is identified by <Person Number>"
"<Person Number> in <Driver> is a subset of <Person Number> in <Person>"

tables.name: Local Area
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A region within a country that groups EU-Rent branches. Cars are owned at local-area level and stored at the branches of that area; a local area is also what an "authorized area" of a rental is expressed in.
[Source]
EU-Rent: "in each country it has local areas containing branches", with "car ownership at the local area level with storage at branches". https://caminao.blog/community/sample-problems/eu-rent-car/
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " lies in <Country of Local Area_Country Code><EU-Rent Network_Local Area Code>"
[Rules]
"<Local Area> is identified by <Local Area Code>"
"<Country Code> in <Local Area> is a subset of <Country Code> in <Country>"

tables.name: One-Way Rental
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A rental whose drop-off branch differs from its pick-up branch. Subtype of Rental, derived rather than asserted: it follows from comparing the two Branch roles. It attracts a location penalty charge (R09).
[Derivation]
One-Way Rental := Rental R WHERE Pick Up Branch[R].Branch <> Drop Off Branch[R].Branch. Never asserted: it follows from the two Branch roles (R09).
tables.verbalization:
[Rules]
"<One-Way Rental> is identified by <Rental Number>"
"<One-Way Rental> is a subset of <Rental Number> in <Rental>"

tables.name: Open Rental
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A rental that has been picked up but not yet returned - state Open. The subject of the Area of Usage Rule (R10): only an open rental has a car out on the road that can leave its authorized area.
[Source]
"open rental" is used as a term in the SBVR EU-Rent rule statements quoted at https://www.brcommunity.com/articles.php?id=c009
[Derivation]
Open Rental := Rental R WHERE Rental State[R].Rental Status = 'Open'. Never asserted: it follows from the state (R10, R11).
tables.verbalization:
[Rules]
"<Open Rental> is identified by <Rental Number>"
"<Open Rental> is a subset of <Rental Number> in <Rental>"

tables.name: Person
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A human being known to EU-Rent. Person is the supertype: the same person may be a customer, a driver, or both. Every person must be at least one of the two - a totality constraint spans the Customer and Driver roles.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is named <Name of Person_Person Name><EU-Rent Parties_Person Number>"
  " was born on <Date of Birth_Birth Date><EU-Rent Parties_Person Number>"
[Rules]
"<Person> is identified by <Person Number>"
"<Person Number> in <Person> is a subset of <Customer> and/or <Person Number> in <Driver>"

tables.name: Rental
tables.comment:
[Definition]
An agreement under which EU-Rent provides a car of a requested car group to a customer for a period, from a pick-up branch to a drop-off branch. The central object type of the model: nearly every business rule is about a rental.
[Example]
Rental 10001: contracted by customer 1001, group B requested, picked up at AMS01 on 2026-09-01, dropped off at BRU01 on 2026-09-05, fulfilled with NL-34-DEF-5. One-way, so it incurs a location penalty charge.
[Source]
EU-Rent case study, OMG SBVR Annex. Overviews: https://kdmanalytics.com/sbvr/EU-Rent.html , https://caminao.blog/community/sample-problems/eu-rent-car/ . EU-Rent was originally developed by Model Systems Ltd. and popularised by the Business Rules Group.
tables.verbalization:
[Expressions]
  " is driven by <Main Driver of Rental_Person Number><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " is dropped off at <Drop Off Branch_Branch Code><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " is fulfilled with <Car of Rental_Registration Number><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " runs from <Rental Period_Pick Up Date> until <Rental Period_Return Date><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " is contracted by <Renter of Rental_Person Number><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " requests <Requested Car Group_Car Group Code><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " is in state <Rental State_Rental Status><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " is picked up at <Pick Up Branch_Branch Code><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
  " was actually returned on <Actual Return Date><EU-Rent Rental Process_Rental Number>"
[Rules]
"<Rental> is identified by <Rental Number>"
"<Person Number> in <Rental> is a subset of <Customer>"
"<Car Group Code> in <Rental> is a subset of <Car Group Code> in <Car Group>"
"<Branch Code> in <Rental> is a subset of <Branch Code> in <Branch>"
"<Branch Code> in <Rental> is a subset of <Branch Code> in <Branch>"

tables.verbalization:

[Rules]

[Expressions]

tables.name: Walk-in Rental
tables.comment:
[Definition]
A rental contracted at the branch counter on the pick-up date itself, with no prior booking. Subtype of Rental. It goes straight to state Open, skipping the Requested state.
[Derivation]
Walk-in Rental := Rental R WHERE Rental State[R] entered 'Open' without ever having been 'Requested' - i.e. the rental was contracted on Rental Period[R].Pick Up Date itself. Needs the state history (transaction time on Rental State) to be evaluated exactly; approximated as NOT Advance Rental at the moment of contracting.
tables.verbalization:
[Rules]
"<Walk-in Rental> is identified by <Rental Number>"
"<Walk-in Rental> is a subset of <Rental Number> in <Rental>"
